# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Before you build anything:**
- Audit what you're *actually* selling right now (classes, 1-on-1, nutrition, challenges, etc.). Ask your top 3 coaches: "What do members ask for that we don't have a clear price for?" This reveals gaps faster than guessing.

**Structure it in two separate documents (not one combined menu):**
- **Member menu**: Pricing, duration, what they get (e.g., "Unlimited classes + 2 coach consultations/month"). Use simple language, no gym jargon. Include a comparison table so they can pick their tier without decision paralysis.
- **Coach menu**: Service definitions, delivery method, commission/pay structure, what they promise clients (e.g., "Form checks included in all sessions," "Nutrition guidance requires additional certification"). Coaches need to know what they're accountable for.

**Pricing logic — use this now:**
- List your monthly fixed costs (rent, insurance, staff) and divide by projected member headcount. Your base tier price must cover that baseline. Then add value tiers above it. Don't undercut; you're women's-only and specialized — price accordingly.

**Get it tested this week:**
- Share the member menu with 5 current members. Ask: "Would you pick this tier? What's missing?" Adjust, then share the coach version with your team. Their pushback = real operational problems to solve before launch.

**Launch with clear ownership:**
- Assign one person (ideally you) as the single source of truth for updates. When pricing or offerings change, one document gets updated first, then communicated out.

## REVENUE — URGENT: Member Quality Collapse

• **Your Rev/member has crashed 29% in 2 months** (£137 in Sept → £103 in Oct). Simultaneously, active members rose 11 (Sept to Oct) but revenue *fell* £4.2k. This is classic low-value sign-ups drowning out premium members. **Action: Suspend discount/intro offers immediately; audit Oct intake—are you onboarding at £50/month when Sept baseline was £180/head?** Run a 7-day win-back campaign on Sept cohort (churn was normal at 6.2%) before October leakage accelerates.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May**, then stabilised 3–6%. Oct at 3.9% is *good*, but Sept's 6.2% suggests member satisfaction dipped mid-cycle. **Action: Pull NPS/feedback from Sept joiners within 14 days; tighten onboarding experience (first 2 weeks retention is your churn control valve).** Losing members only hurts if you've paid acquisition cost.

• **Last 3 months (Aug–Oct) average £18.6k revenue vs prior 3 (May–Jul) £17.5k—only +6.3% on flat-to-rising member count (127→172).** You're adding bodies, not value. **Action: Tier your membership (Core £49/m + Premium £79/m with studio hire/PT credits); immediately test a £15/month upsell (class pass 10-pack, retail £80, cost £8 to deliver).** Target: lift Rev/member back to £125 by Dec.

## EXPENSES — Where are they? You're hiding margin.

• **You've given me revenue but no P&L.** On £16–22k monthly revenue, I need to see: staff wages, rent/studio costs, software (TeamUp, GoCardless, Stripe fees ~2%), utilities. **Action: Export your Starling P&L by cost centre (or build one). Once I see fixed costs, I'll identify if studio relocation lifted rent burden—if rent jumped >20% with +35 members (Apr→Oct), it's a drag.** Rule of thumb: staffing should be 35–40% of revenue; rent 20–25%. If you're at 60%+ combined, cost base is killing profit.
